We show that the coefficient tracks the analytical observability determinant of the Lie-derivative approach: it is zero when the determinant vanishes, lies strictly between zero and one when the determinant depends on the state, and equals one when the determinant is a nonzero constant. We apply the method to a seven-state synchronous machine and to the 21-state Western System Coordinating Council nine-bus system under several synchrophasor measurement configurations. On the nine-bus system, the coefficient grows from 0.0952 with one PMU to 0.1905 with two and 0.2857 with three, and the whole analysis runs in under five seconds. Configurations with the same number of PMUs receive the same coefficient, yet an unscented Kalman filter estimates the states with different accuracy for each. The symbolic coefficient therefore grades measurement sets beyond identifying root strongly connected components, while telling PMU locations apart still requires the numerical parameters of the system.

papers.title: Benign Geometry and Distributional Robustness of $\mathcal{H}_2$ Synthesis

papers.title: Human-on-the-Loop Distributed Control of Grid-Interactive Buildings for Demand Response Participation
papers.summary: This paper proposes a human-on-the-loop distributed consensus control approach for demand-side management across multiple buildings. papers.title: Predictive Neuromorphic Control of a Scanning Mirror System: An Event-Centric Framework
papers.summary: Organizing control around events can reduce sensing and actuation demands while directly linking control decisions to the occurrence and timing of desired system behaviors. This paper proposes a novel event-centric model predictive control (MPC) framework that unifies event sensing, event prediction, and event regulation. Events define the feedback information, prediction horizon, and event-timing objectives, placing them at the center of predictive control design. The framework is developed for a scanning mirror system equipped with a baseline neuromorphic controller composed of spiking neurons that supports sparse actuation. The control objective is to achieve prescribed zero-crossing times and a desired scanning range while minimizing the mechanical energy transferred between the actuator and the mirror. A sampling-based algorithm is presented to obtain suboptimal solutions of the event-centric MPC optimization problem without requiring an explicit event-to-event prediction model. By grounding predictive optimization in events, the proposed framework opens a new direction for MPC design and its integration with neuromorphic control.

papers.title: Safe and Scalable Minimax Adaptive Control of Positive Systems
papers.summary: This paper studies minimax adaptive control of positive linear systems with fixed unknown dynamics and nonnegative disturbances. We reformulate the problem by compressing the historical data into a vector and a positivity-induced consistency set containing the models compatible with the observations. Together with the physical state, these quantities form a sufficient information state and yield an exact reformulation as a standard minimax dynamic game. We allow the admissible input set to adapt to the current consistency set, ensuring positivity for every remaining feasible model. As inconsistent models are eliminated, the input set can expand, allowing less cautious control actions. For finite model sets, we derive an explicit solution to the Bellman inequality and construct a safe and stabilizing certainty-equivalence controller with robustness guarantees. The framework also accommodates structured classes of continuum model uncertainty whose consistency sets admit fixed, finite-dimensional representations, enabling scalable information-state updates.

papers.title: Distributionally Robust Indirect-Feedback Stochastic MPC with Gelbrich Ambiguity Sets
papers.summary: Stochastic model predictive control uses disturbance statistics to set safety margins. Errors in these statistics can invalidate the safety guarantees. This paper therefore describes the uncertainty in the disturbance mean and covariance by a prescribed Gelbrich ambiguity set. This contains distributions of any shape whose moments are close in the Gelbrich distance to the nominal values, including distributions with unbounded support. For linear time-invariant systems with additive disturbances, we build on the indirect feedback paradigm, propagate this moment uncertainty along the error dynamics, and obtain a closed-form constraint tightening that is computed offline. Robustness enters as a single additive term that grows with the size of the ambiguity set, so the online problem remains a quadratic program. Recursive feasibility and closed-loop satisfaction of conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) constraints hold for every disturbance distribution in the set. We illustrate the method on a linearized planar quadrotor.

papers.title: Excitable Behaviours of a First-Order High-Pass Neuron Model
papers.summary: With the rise of neuromorphic technologies, simple and tunable neuron models are needed to analyse and design spiking systems. However, the simplest neuron models, e.g., Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) models, usually fail to capture the excitable behaviours of biological neurons. This could be a significant limitation, as excitability enables reliable spike timing under parametric uncertainties. Recently, a minimal excitable model, the so-called High-Pass Model (HPM), was introduced in neuroengineering. It simply consists of a static sigmoid with a high-pass filter in positive feedback. Given its novelty, it is still unclear how easily the HPM can be tuned, and how much of the excitable behaviours of a biophysical neuron it can reproduce. To address these questions, we investigate the tunability of a first-order HPM sub- and supra-rheobase, i.e., below and above the onset of the tonic spiking regime (where the neuron spikes periodically), and compare its behaviours with those of a simple Hodgkin-Huxley-type Conductance-Based Model (CBM). Below rheobase, both models fire spikes in response to transient inputs, including post-inhibitory rebound spikes. Above rheobase, an affine reparametrization of the input of the HPM suffices to fit its frequency-current curve to that of a CBM. The two models mostly differ near their respective rheobases, where the first-order HPM lacks bistability and spike latency. We suggest that modifying the frequency-selective element of the HPM may be sufficient to overcome this limitation. These results highlight the potential of the HPM as a fundamental computational primitive in neuromorphic, spike-based technologies.

papers.title: An extended Perron-Frobenius operator filter for nonlinear state estimation
papers.summary: We propose an extended Perron--Frobenius Operator Filter (PFOF) for nonlinear state estimation. The method learns the Perron--Frobenius operator, an infinite-dimensional linear operator fully preserving properties of a nonlinear dynamical system, using the extended Dynamic Mode Decomposition (eDMD). This enables us to explicitly account for non-Gaussian distributions exhibited by the nonlinear system within a linear-operator representation, while retaining the freedom to choose basis functions in eDMD. Through two numerical examples, we show that the extended PFOF achieves high computational efficiency and high estimation accuracy by exploiting the flexibility in the choice of basis functions in eDMD.

papers.title: Safety and Connectivity Certificates for Finite-Time Formation Transitions
papers.summary: Finite-time formation transitions are useful for coordinating multi-agent systems in time-critical missions, but convergence to a prescribed formation in finite time does not guarantee collision avoidance or communication connectivity during the transition. Existing approaches address finite-time coordination and safety-constrained formation control, yet explicit connections between disagreement during transitions, formation geometry, and coupling-gain selection need to be developed for certifying safe maneuvers. This paper develops a disagreement-based framework for certifying transient safety and connectivity during finite-time tracking of arbitrary prescribed formation trajectories. Local feedback guarantees exact finite-time tracking with a graph-independent settling-time bound, while a graph-dependent disagreement bound is used to derive sufficient geometric conditions for collision avoidance and connectivity preservation. These conditions further yield an offline coupling-gain selection rule based on the available geometric clearance. Numerical simulations illustrate the trade-off between convergence rate and control effort as the coupling gain increases. They also demonstrate the effectiveness and conservatism of the proposed certificates.

papers.title: Online Adaptive Clustering in Robust Distributed Model Predictive Control
papers.summary: This paper proposes a dynamic clustering framework for tube-based model predictive control (MPC) of coupled multi-agent systems. Agents within a cluster coordinate their dynamics explicitly, while couplings from agents outside the cluster are treated as bounded disturbances. For each admissible cluster, we construct a state-dependent mismatch measure from a robust upper bound on its predicted closed-loop cost and an optimistic, partition-independent lower bound. Combining this mismatch with a communication penalty enables online selection of the clustering topology, ranging from centralized to fully decentralized operation. The resulting switching controller is shown to preserve recursive feasibility and constraint satisfaction, and to render the closed-loop system practically asymptotically stable. Furthermore, the mismatch provides an upper bound on the finite-horizon performance difference with respect to centralized MPC. An eight-agent spring--damper example illustrates how the controller adapts cooperation while maintaining performance close to centralized MPC with reduced communication.

papers.title: The Role of Insurance in Power-System Risk Management: A Critical Review
papers.summary: Modern power systems are becoming more renewable-rich, digitalized, and interconnected, making risk propagation and economic consequences increasingly complex. Physical mitigation remains the primary means of risk control, but technical and economic limits leave residual risk. Insurance can complement these measures by transferring associated economic losses and influencing power-system decisions through risk-responsive terms. Despite growing interest, the literature remains fragmented across power-system engineering, actuarial science, and risk finance. This review develops an integrated physical-financial perspective for reviewing insurance in power systems. It examines how power system risks generate residual economic losses and the conditions under which these losses can be insured and transferred. It then develops an actuarial framework for insured-loss assessment and pricing. Insurance-aware decision-making is synthesized through four coupling levels describing how financial protection interacts with power-system decisions. Further progress is constrained by weak physical-financial loss validation, incomplete representation of systemic and evolving portfolio risk, and limited empirical and actuarial grounding of insurance-decision feedback. Research priorities include stronger physical-financial data linkage, forward-looking portfolio assessment, multi-timescale decision feedback, and empirical validation. Addressing these priorities would help move power-system insurance from fragmented applications toward a more coherent approach to residual-risk management in future power systems.

papers.title: Towards Mode-Balanced Intersection Control: Hierarchical Coordination of Signal Timings, AV Trajectories, and Cyclist Speed Advice
papers.summary: Connected and automated vehicles (AVs) enable traffic signals and vehicle trajectories to be optimised jointly, but existing co-optimisation frameworks overlook cyclists, even though they share the same intersections. The upper level jointly optimises signal timings and cyclist speed advice, while the lower level optimises AV trajectories and also updates cyclist speed advice obtained from the higher level at a higher frequency based on the resulting signal plan. The framework is evaluated in simulation under multiple demand profiles and optimisation parameter settings. Compared with optimized vehicle trajectories with fixed-time signal control, the proposed framework reduces mean travel times by 13.6\% for AVs and 12.3\% for cyclists. Adding cyclist speed advice further reduces mean cyclist waiting time by about 80\% relative to the same framework without speed advice. These results demonstrate substantial benefits for both modes of transport.

papers.title: Towards Design of Efficient Neuromorphic Controllers
papers.summary: One of the major sources of inspiration for neuromorphic engineering is the central nervous system, which is orders of magnitude more efficient than classical digital clock-based computers. papers.title: Explicit MPC for the constrained zonotope case with low-rank matrix updates
papers.summary: Solving the explicit Model Predictive Control (MPC) problem requires enumerating all critical regions and their associated feedback laws, a task that scales exponentially with the system dimension and the prediction horizon, as well. When the problem's constraints are boxes or zonotopes, the feasible domain admits a compact constrained-zonotope representation. Building on this insight, we exploit the geometric properties of the equivalent constrained-zonotope reformulation to accelerate the computation of the explicit solution. Specifically, we formulate the multi-parametric problem in the lifted generator space and solve it using second-order optimality conditions, employ low-rank matrix updates to reduce computation time, and introduce an analytic enumeration of candidate active sets that yields the explicit solution in tree form.

papers.title: Neuromodulation Through Intrinsic Noise
papers.summary: Neuromodulation, the modulation of excitability through the regulation of neuronal parameters, is a key tool in neuromorphic control design. This paper investigates how spiking excitability can be modulated by intrinsic noise. Focusing on a simplified memristive neuron model, we show that intrinsic noise plays distinct functional roles depending on the feedback pathways: Intrinsic noise in the fast excitatory feedback shapes the nature of excitability and modulates the sensitivity of the neuron to external/internal stimuli, whereas that in the slow inhibitory feedback provides internal stimuli that can trigger stochastic spiking. We expect these findings to guide the design of neuromorphic systems that harness intrinsic noise to exploit beneficial stochastic phenomena, such as stochastic resonance.

papers.title: Continuous-Time Modeling of Destination-Constrained Dynamic Systems via Doob's $h$-Transform
papers.summary: Existing work on modeling destination-constrained dynamic systems has mainly focused on discrete-time formulations with linear destination constraints or Gaussian destination distributions. Since practical systems are more naturally modeled in continuous time and often subject to nonlinear/non-Gaussian constraints/distributions, this paper proposes a unified measure-transformation framework for continuous-time modeling of systems subject to deterministic or distributional constraints on a nonlinear function of the terminal state. The framework starts from an unconstrained Itô stochastic differential equation, typically derived from physical laws to describe the system's forward evolution without destination information, and takes its induced path measure as unconstrained measure. Doob's $h$-transform is employed to transform this measure into a constrained path measure incorporating destination information through an injected drift. The resulting system is proved to satisfy the constraints while preserving the laws of the unconstrained state process conditioned on the destination information. The transition density is derived, and the path measure of the distributionally constrained system is proved to uniquely minimize Kullback--Leibler divergence from the unconstrained path measure among those satisfying the same distributional constraint. Its injected drift is further shown to converge pointwise to that of the deterministically constrained system as the destination distribution shrinks to the prespecified value. For linear time-varying unconstrained systems, a simplified form of the constrained systems is derived in terms of the conditional expectation of the terminal state, leading to the development of trajectory-generation algorithms. Numerical simulations evaluate the proposed framework under both types of destination constraints.

papers.title: Aeroelastically Constrained Optimal Path Planning of a Fixed-Wing Airborne Wind Energy System
papers.summary: Multi-megawatt fixed-wing airborne wind energy systems (AWES) use an aircraft with large, slender wings that deform over the pumping cycle. To harvest maximum energy, the cycle is usually designed by means of dedicated reference trajectory optimization routines. It is well known that such routines rely heavily on the system model and that close alignment between the model and the physical system is required for the results to hold in practice. Nevertheless, the wing is usually treated as rigid and structural limits are respected indirectly through upper bounding of states and inputs. In this work, we directly enforce bounds on the elastic deflection and twist of the wing in the power-maximizing periodic optimal control problem. To that end, we model the wing by root-clamped modes, loaded by strip-theory aerodynamics and by the gravitational and inertial loads of the manoeuvring aircraft. To keep the problem tractable, the modal dynamics are replaced by their quasi-static equilibrium, which enters every discretization interval as algebraic constraints. For a multi-megawatt reference aircraft, the elastic twist near the wing tips reaches $1.03^\circ$ along the optimal rigid-wing trajectory. With a twist limit of $0.6^\circ$, the optimal trajectory delivers $31\,\%$ less mean power than the rigid-wing one, mainly through a lower tether tension during reel-out. Rigid-wing trajectory optimization can thus overestimate the power that the wing limits permit. Forward simulations that retain the modal dynamics demonstrate that the quasi-static deflection and twist deviate from the dynamic ones by less than $2\,\%$ of their limits. This work shows that elastic deformation can be accounted for in the trajectory optimization and that, depending on the wing limits, it can strongly reduce the achievable power.

papers.title: Priority-Aware Firm and Flexible Capacity Quantification for Large-Load Interconnection
papers.summary: We study how to unlock existing transmission capacity to accelerate large-load interconnection under differentiated quality-of-service (QoS) requirements. papers.title: An Accurate Modulation-Assisted Method for Phasor Estimation Under Decaying DC Offsets
papers.summary: Decaying DC (DDC) offsets severely compromise the accurate estimation of current phasors immediately following power grid fault occurrence. Consequently, conventional full-cycle discrete Fourier transform (FCDFT) algorithms experience decaying oscillatory magnitude errors, potentially causing distance relays to malfunction. This paper introduces a modulation-assisted technique designed to precisely eliminate the DDC components from fault current signals. By multiplying the fault signal with a high-frequency carrier and applying consecutive sliding Fourier projections, the proposed method effectively isolates the DDC signal while entirely rejecting higher-order harmonic interference. It utilizes a direct algebraic solution derived from a robust forward-difference operation across just three sequential projections to estimate and extract the DDC parameters. Furthermore, the algorithm seamlessly processes both single and multiple DDC components by dynamically tracking them as one equivalent first-order mode. Extensive evaluations are conducted to validate the proposed method accuracy. The proposed algorithm limits the maximum overshoot (MO) to 0.62% (0.59% for $k \geq 8$) for the evaluated DDC cases, and to 2.47% (0.95% at 20 dB for $k = 8$) under noisy conditions.

papers.title: Incremental Input-to-State Stabilization of Partially Unknown Control-Affine Systems within Prescribed Safe Sets
papers.summary: Incremental input-to-state stability ($δ$-ISS) guarantees that the trajectories of a system converge towards one another, up to a gain on the difference of their inputs. Some existing learning-based designs that combine incremental stability with safety achieve only incremental input-to-state practical stability, whose non-vanishing offset can make the guarantee conservative. We consider control-affine systems with a known, full-row-rank input matrix and an unknown drift learned using Gaussian process regression. The prescribed safe set is a superlevel set of a smooth function satisfying a radial condition that ensures a diffeomorphism onto $\mathbb R^n$ and it need not contain any equilibrium of the uncontrolled system. Using this transformation, we design a smooth feedback law and derive sufficient conditions that, under the stated learning assumptions, guarantee with high probability both forward invariance of a compact subset of the safe set and $δ$-ISS on that subset. The incremental estimate uses the distance induced by the transformation and contains no practical offset. Simulations on a Van der Pol oscillator and a Lotka-Volterra system illustrate the proposed approach.

papers.title: Data-Driven Robust Dynamic Wireless Charging Lane Planning with Tunable Profit--Risk Trade-off and Modified User Equilibrium
papers.summary: Dynamic wireless charging (DWC) has attracted increasing attention as a complement to conventional plug-in charging for electric vehicles (EVs). A data-driven uncertainty set is constructed from joint historical scenarios to preserve spatio-temporal correlations without imposing parametric distributional assumptions. A modified user-equilibrium (MUE) model is proposed to capture realistic EV routing and charging behavior by incorporating state-of-charge (SoC) dynamics and endogenous charging decisions. An \textit{a posteriori} feasibility guarantee is established to quantify out-of-sample risk. Based on this guarantee, the scenario set is iteratively enriched to meet a prescribed risk tolerance. Case studies on a 69-node power distribution network and a 24-node traffic network demonstrate that the proposed MUE model prevents overinvestment in DWCLs, while the proposed risk-quantification procedure enables a tunable profit--risk trade-off.

papers.title: Impact of Reduced-Order Modelling on Sum-of-Squares Region-of-Attraction Certification for Grid-Forming and Grid-Following Converters
papers.summary: With the increasing penetration of power-electronic equipment, the transient stability of grid-forming (GFM) and grid-following (GFL) converters is increasingly characterized through the region of attraction (ROA) of the post-fault equilibrium. Sum-of-squares (SOS) programming yields certified inner approximations of the ROA, yet its computational cost grows rapidly with system order. Reduced-order models are therefore widely used to reduce computational cost and, more importantly, to enable analytical investigation. However, ROA analyses based on these models often assume that reproducing the converter's transient response, or retaining more dynamics in the correct time-frame, is sufficient to preserve the ROA of the full-order system. Using time-domain ODE simulations as a reference, the SOS-based ROA of each reduced-order GFM and GFL model is assessed against both its own simulated ROA and that of the corresponding full-order model, thereby separating SOS-induced conservativeness from model-order-induced ROA distortion. The results indicate that increasing reduced-order model complexity does not necessarily improve SOS-based ROA fidelity. In the cases examined, more complex reduced-order models yield lower SOS coverage of the full-order reference ROA, despite closer ODE-boundary agreement in some regions. Model selection should therefore consider both full-order ROA fidelity and certified coverage of the practical operating range, rather than model complexity alone.

papers.title: Complete Decentralization of Wave Equation Control on a Compact Domain
papers.summary: A feedback control policy is completely decentralized if the actuation signal at each location in space can be computed based only on state information from that location. For systems equipped with large numbers of spatially distributed sensors and actuators, completely decentralized controllers are desirable since they can be implemented in a communication and computation efficient manner, but generally perform worse than centralized counterparts. However, through a case study of Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) design for wave dynamics on a compact spatial domain, we show that careful design of system parameters to satisfy certain conditions causes a decentralized control policy to perform as well as any centralized policy. We then propose a spatially filtered $H_2$ norm to show that satisfying these conditions does not inherently degrade achievable closed-loop system performance, enabling simultaneous realization of both desirable performance and communication/computation efficiency via system-control co-design. Additional robustness analysis characterizes a range of system parameters such that the system interconnected with a decentralized controller maintains stability and near-optimal performance. Although our framework is derived for spatially continuous dynamics, we demonstrate that this theory can be leveraged to derive results for decentralization in finite-dimensional settings through a damped mass-spring example.

papers.title: Residual-Corrected Physics-Informed Neural Network KKL Observers with Input-to-State Stability Guarantees
papers.summary: Physics-informed neural network (PINN) Kazantzis--Kravaris--Luenberger (KKL) observers require an approximate solution to a KKL partial differential equation (PDE) and an approximate inverse of this solution. We build an encoder containing an explicitly invertible neural map. Its closed-form inverse provides the internal state reconstruction used to evaluate the learned KKL residual and correct the latent dynamics. This construction makes the synchronization manifold exactly invariant for every value of the network weights. Based on contraction of the residual-corrected observer dynamics, we prove an input-to-state stability (ISS) result for the implemented error dynamics with respect to measurement noise. A direct consequence is that the estimation error converges exponentially to zero in the noise-free setting. We provide two numerical examples, the Van der Pol oscillator and the chaotic Lorenz system, in which the residual-corrected observers achieve exact noise-free convergence and improved error responses compared with released PINN--KKL baselines.

papers.title: A Global Routing Method for Electronic Circuit Design Integrating Flow Matching and Constrained A*
papers.summary: Global routing is a fundamental issue in the design of electronic circuits, as it directly relates to the efficiency, reliability, and compactness of the overall layout of integrated systems. As the demand for higher functionality and reliability within a limited chip area increases, the importance of routing as a design consideration has never been greater. Efficient global routing optimization techniques are therefore required to connect all pins with minimal wirelength (WL), while avoiding congestion and interference across multiple nets within the design space. As the number of nets to be routed increases, global routing inherently suffers from a combinatorial explosion in the design space, making it increasingly difficult to obtain feasible solutions. In this paper, we focus on solving constrained global routing problems based on a heuristic A*-based framework. Based on this concept, a hybrid approach is proposed by integrating constrained A* with flow matching (FM). The method utilizes FM to construct a global cost map that captures routing tendencies across the design space, which is then used to guide the constrained A* search process. This enables efficient exploration of the solution space while satisfying routing constraints. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves comparable WL and via usage to baseline methods while maintaining constraint satisfaction across a wide range of scenarios. Notably, the framework shows strong capability in solving complex routing instances that are difficult to handle using conventional approaches. Additionally, the method shows robust generalization performance across different problem sizes and net configurations.

papers.title: Spurious-Free Lithium Niobate Bulk Acoustic Wave Resonator with Grounded-Ring Electrode
papers.summary: High-performance piezoelectric resonators are promising energy-storage elements for piezoelectric power conversion because of their compact footprint and low loss at frequencies where conventional magnetic components become bulky and inefficient. These results establish the grounded-ring TE-mode LN BAW resonator as a practical platform for piezoelectric power conversion and a broader design approach for realizing high-performance spurious-free acoustic resonators.

papers.title: Repeated Binary Direct Collinear Impacts Under Incremental Contact Laws With Residual Indentation: A Hybrid Systems Formulation
papers.summary: Incremental contact laws specify the normal contact force through a differential relation, possibly carrying an internal state, driven by the indentation and its rate. The force may vanish at a nonzero indentation, through plasticity, an elastic aftereffect, or, under some laws with a viscous component, a load drawing the bodies apart rapidly, leaving a residual deformation at separation. Such a deformation sits uneasily within rigid body dynamics, which admits none. The tension is tolerable when the indentation is small relative to the bodies, so that it may be carried constitutively rather than geometrically. Even then, the law alone does not determine the interaction: because force and indentation no longer vanish together, conditions for the commencement and termination of contact must be supplied separately, as must the fate of the deformation and internal state at separation, both absent from the equations of motion. This article formulates the repeated direct collinear impact of two convex bodies under external forces as a hybrid dynamical system. The contact interface is modeled as a massless element carrying the contact law and its state, coupled to the bodies through relative velocity and an interaction force dictated by the contact state. Consequently, all switching and resets are confined to the interface, leaving the geometry and equations of motion of the bodies unaltered. The principal analytical properties of the formulations are established, among them passivity and completeness; the branching of solutions at the onset and termination of contact is examined. The framework is demonstrated through numerical simulations.

Where two intended trajectories conflict, an order gate, a precedence network distilled from a right-of-way rule, decides who goes first; both vehicles evaluate it on the same messages and so reach the same order. When2Go imitates the rule-based expert of V2Xverse, which sees the simulator's ground truth; stops that When2Go cannot observe within its 2 s planning horizon are relabelled, so that it does not learn to wait without an observable cause. For our runs only, the benchmarks' PID controller steers by When2Go's waypoints instead of the route, and its forced push of long-waiting vehicles is off. With one model, When2Go sets the state of the art on three closed-loop CARLA benchmarks: 97.8 and 90.7 driving score on InterDrive without and with traffic (best published 90.1 and 78.9), 70.0 on the public V2Xverse protocol (best of sixteen rerun methods 59.1) and 88.2 on MDrive (best rerun 85.1), with 95.0% of its vehicles collision-free (87.7%).

papers.title: Breaking survivorship bias in driving world models
papers.summary: World models allow autonomous vehicles to imagine the consequences of candidate actions before execution, but their reliability depends on the futures represented in their training data. We identify a survivorship bias in driving world models: because the futures recorded in prevailing driving datasets almost always end safely, existing models often imagine benign outcomes even when a collision is imminent. We introduce a neutral world model (NWM) that learns both routine and safety-critical futures from a mixture of routine driving and real accident videos with a bounding-box-guided objective. The NWM more faithfully anticipates imminent collisions, while maintaining a low false collision rate and competitive generation quality in routine driving. We further use the model as an imagination engine for decision-making. Given multiple ego trajectories, the NWM predicts the future associated with each candidate, and a reward function evaluates these imagined outcomes before selecting an action. On challenging NAVSIM scenarios, this procedure selects the better trajectory more reliably than the baseline world model. Zero-shot experiments with real-world pedestrian dummy crossing data collected using an autonomous research vehicle further demonstrate transfer to unseen sensor observations. These results show that correcting survivorship bias enables world models to more faithfully reason about futures and support safety-critical decision-making in autonomous driving.

papers.title: Towards Robust Vision-Language Reasoning: A Multi-Stage Optimization Pipeline with Masked Diffusion Model
papers.summary: Discrete diffusion generation is emerging as a competitive alternative to autoregressive generation by denoising the entire token sequence through iterative refinement. papers.title: Distill to Think, Foresee to Act: Cognitive-Physical Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Driving
papers.summary: Current end-to-end autonomous driving models are fundamentally constrained by the behavioral cloning ceiling of imitation learning. Built upon this dual infrastructure, we optimize the driving policy via GRPO with a novel dual-reward mechanism: a physical reward derived from BEV rollouts enforces hard safety constraints, while a cognitive reward from a language-aligned scorer ensures intent compliance. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CoPhy not only achieves state-of-the-art results on NAVSIM v1 and v2 benchmarks, but also enables safer driving via cognitively informed scene compliance and flexible intent control through user-defined language instructions. papers.title: Multi-Agent Conditional Diffusion Planning for Decentralized Wireless Resource Allocation
papers.summary: In wireless communication systems, efficient and adaptive resource allocation is essential for enhancing overall Quality of Service (QoS). Compared with conventional Model-Free Reinforcement Learning (MFRL), Model-Based RL (MBRL) first learns a generative world model for subsequent planning, enabling more stable training through the reuse of historical experience. However, deploying MBRL in large-scale wireless networks remains challenging due to high-dimensional stochastic dynamics, strong inter-agent cooperation, and stringent communication constraints. To overcome these challenges, we propose a Multi-Agent Conditional Diffusion Model Planner (MA-CDMP) for decentralized communication resource management. Following the Decentralized Training with Decentralized Execution (DTDE) paradigm, MA-CDMP models each communication node as an autonomous agent and employs Diffusion Models (DMs) to capture environment dynamics. An inverse dynamics model is further incorporated to guide action generation, improving sample efficiency and policy scalability. Moreover, to efficiently approximate large-scale agent interactions, we introduce a Mean Field (MF) mechanism to assist the classifier in conditional DMs. This mitigates inter-agent non-stationarity and enhances cooperation with minimal communication overhead. We further establish an upper bound on the distributional approximation error induced by MF-based diffusion generation, guaranteeing convergence stability and reliable modeling of multi-agent stochastic dynamics. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MA-CDMP consistently outperforms existing MARL baselines in terms of average reward and QoS metrics, showcasing its scalability and practicality for real-world wireless network optimization.

papers.title: Evaluating Video LLMs' Understanding of Corner Cases in Autonomous Driving
papers.summary: Natural language explanations promised by modern Video Large Language Models (Video LLMs) offer autonomous driving systems a path toward detailed scene description and interpretable decision making on the road. papers.title: Medical Image Segmentation: Foundation Model Adaptation versus Task-Specific Training
papers.summary: Foundation models pretrained on large natural-image collections are increasingly adapted for medical image segmentation, in the expectation that they will replace models trained for each task. Most comparisons, however, use data from the training distribution and a single task-specific baseline whose configuration is rarely justified, and therefore provide limited evidence of performance at new clinical sites. It also remains unclear how much of a foundation model must be adapted, and what determines this. We adapted a foundation model, DINOv2, with strategies ranging from tuning only its bias terms to full fine-tuning, and compared it with U-Nets and ResU-Nets trained from scratch. Experiments covered colonoscopy, breast ultrasound and dermoscopy, with testing on held-out data from the training source and on independent datasets from other institutions. The adapted foundation model generalised better on every external dataset. Within the training distribution, the task-specific models remained competitive when training data were abundant, and delineated boundaries more precisely, while the foundation model more often missed small lesions. Only a small fraction of the foundation model required adaptation, and the capacity needed was determined by the imaging domain rather than by the adaptation method. A widely used polyp test set was also found to duplicate images from another benchmark. Foundation-model adaptation is therefore warranted where models must work across sites, with capacity selected on the target domain.

papers.title: Counterfactual Analysis of Extent Leakage from Annotation-Derived Prompts in Vision-Language Medical Image Segmentation
papers.summary: Text-guided segmentation models receive an image and a short caption about the lesion, and on public benchmarks the caption improves accuracy considerably. On colonoscopy and breast ultrasound, however, the size, count and location words of each caption were computed from the mask that later scores the prediction, and the chest X-ray captions were written by benchmark annotators. We tested what two published models take from them. On colonoscopy and chest X-ray, it is mostly the lesion's extent. Keeping only the size word or the lung-zone phrase recovers 84 to 98 percent of the improvement over an empty caption, and removing it loses 52 to 77 percent. The rest matters little, and a polyp called a rock is segmented just as well. We call this extent leakage. On breast ultrasound, nearly half the captions also name the diagnosis, which carries part of the benefit. Retraining on three datasets shows that models pick up this habit from their training captions, though only partly on breast ultrasound, and that it weakens their segmentation from the image alone. The leak can be measured without training a model, since caption words alone predict lesion area (coefficient of determination 0.54 to 0.77 on six of seven test sets). Without the test mask, the best method we tested, which estimates extent from the image, reaches 74.59 Dice on colonoscopy against the published 77.23. We propose an evaluation protocol that keeps what a caption says about the image apart from what it copies from the label.

papers.title: From Foundation VLM to Versatile Driving VLM: A Triplet Incremental Training Approach

papers.title: Achieving Robust Channel Estimation Neural Networks on Doppler effects by Designed Training Data
papers.summary: Channel estimation is crucial in wireless communication systems. Many existing works train and test their models using the same or similar channel. However, practical channels are infinitely diverse and time-variant while data-driven algorithms often degrade on new and previously unseen channels. This prohibits the practical implementation of neural networks for channel estimation, particularly in high speed scenarios characterized by rapidly channel profile changes and very high Doppler shifts. Online training can fine-tune models to adapt to new channels, but requires high computation resource and incurs significant latency for physical-layer devices. Moreover, online training cannot exhaustively cover all possible channels because there are infinitely many possible channels. Therefore, we investigate the ability of neural networks to generalize to wireless channels. This paper proposes design criteria to generate synthetic training data, which guaranty that the resulting networks perform robustly across wireless channels, especially for very high Doppler shifts and different Doppler spectra. It ensures that offline-trained neural networks require no prior information or online training to precisely estimate the new channels. To demonstrate general applicability, we use neural networks with different levels of complexity to show that the generalization achieved appears to be independent of architecture. From simulation results, neural networks achieve a certain performance across wireless channels with different unseen power delay profiles (PDP) and Doppler shifts.

papers.title: Mitigating SM-Level Load Imbalance in 3D Gaussian Splatting on GPUs
papers.summary: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables photorealistic, real-time rendering on commodity GPUs and is increasingly adopted in generative world models and autonomous driving simulators. Our approach uses a persistent kernel to schedule heavy tiles first and selectively chunks outlier tiles across multiple CTAs. A lightweight per-frame policy determines when and how much to chunk using tile statistics already available in the rendering pipeline. Our approach requires neither retraining nor specialized hardware and can be applied orthogonally to existing optimizations across diverse 3DGS variants. Averaged per scene, it accelerates alpha blending by up to 2.93x on a large-scale urban scene, and by up to 5.6x on its most imbalanced frames, while retaining the original alpha blending formulation.

papers.title: From matrix inversion to constraints: provably tighter confidence regions for importance weights in label shift
papers.summary: Importance weights are essential in domain adaptation under label shift, yet their utility is often undermined by the finite sample uncertainty associated with their estimation. We use this framework to define a joint confidence region and extract marginal intervals via linear programming, deriving provably tighter bounds for importance weights while maintaining exact finite-sample validity.
